canonical_data: research questions, peer workspaces, experiment code, evaluation outputs, evidence, lineage, and generation summaries
current_repo_note: PRAXIST is in beta. Its public source is governed by a Fair Source license with internal-use, distribution, revenue, and commercial-license restrictions, so it is not classified as open source.
strengths: Treats executable evaluation and durable evidence as part of the research loop rather than relying only on generated prose
Parallel peers and generation-to-generation synthesis support broad exploration without discarding lineage
Local workspaces expose artifacts, code, results, and failure evidence for review
weaknesses: Beta maturity and a small operating history limit confidence in long-running reliability
High-autonomy parallel research can consume substantial model, compute, and reviewer attention
The Fair Source terms restrict distribution and some commercial use despite public source availability
why_it_matters: A distinctive research-agent design centered on falsifiable, computer-executable evidence and evolutionary parallel search rather than a single linear report workflow.
